discharged: In arbitrary rank, native simple-root lifting and Mathlib adjugates construct a strict Frobenius basis; the adapted ideal-power argument makes actual tame inertia diagonal.

The original embedding square gives an open finite restriction kernel; native residue Frobenius generation then decomposes the whole actual finite local representation into unit-valued characters, with cyclic inertia and coordinate equations b^p=b.

The native selected-prime construction retains its explicit split torus witness through the dimension-bounded family killing the original dual Selmer group. An actual original norm-residue Frobenius has that same finite conjugacy class.

At these selected primes the local consumer derives residual inertia triviality, the residue characteristic, p different from q, p=1 in the residue field, distinct weights, and the coefficient eigenbasis.

For an actual continuous global Artinian deformation into discrete coefficients, the existing finite Galois factorization constructs the finite number field, local restriction and commuting embedding square. The resulting character theorem applies to the whole original local restriction, allowing an enlarged ramification set.
boundary: Actual modular residual representation, prime-field coefficient realization and the SL2 image required by prime selection remain open. The global character consumer assumes the actual continuous Artinian deformation and its literal local reduction compatibility; it does not assume a finite factor, inertia triviality or a diagonal Frobenius basis. Complete local-ring realization with Delta_Q action and quotient comparison, crystalline conditions, arithmetic Hecke comparison, automorphy and higher continuation remain open.
